title: God of Our Fathers! by Whose Hand
description: God of Our Fathers! by Whose Hand in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 68, “For Guidance and Protection”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God of our fa-thers! by whose hand Thy peo-ple still are blest, Be with us through our pil-grim-age, Con-duct us to our rest.

lines: God of our fathers! by whose hand
Be with us through our pilgrimage,
Through each perplexing path of life
Give us each day our daily bread,
O, spread Thy sheltering wings around,
And at our Fathers loved abode
To Thee, our Father and our God,
And thankful own, that all we are
And all we have is Thine.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
